subject: Connectiva onramp: architecture recap & network prerequisites
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@connectiva.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@connectiva.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: onramp architecture + networking prerequisites

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the Connectiva team. Below is a short recap and concrete networking/auth asks so your infra team can unblock evaluation. I focused the list on what our integration engineering will need to prove a private-onramp POC.

Key deliverables we discussed
- SDK setup: customer will use Redwood JS SDK from a VPC-hosted application with server-side calls. We support mTLS and short-lived token exchange (OIDC) for private endpoints.
- Structured output/tool calling: we’ll surface the tool-calling endpoint and a JSON schema contract for your reranker + downstream actioner.
- Embeddings/rerank: initial plan is to call embeddings from an isolated endpoint and run a lightweight reranker in your infra using the embedding vectors we provide.

Networking / private connectivity asks (high priority)
1) VPC Endpoint: please provision a private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink or GCP Serverless VPC connector equivalent) to allow outbound-to-Redwood over private IPs.
2) Egress & IP allowlist: if PrivateLink not available, we will provide a small set of egress IPs to allowlist. Expect an initial set of four IPs for the dev pool and a larger set for prod.
3) DNS: Ensure private DNS/forwarding so your app resolves the redwood-hostnames to the private endpoint; if using PrivateLink, enable private hosted zone takeover.
4) mTLS and/or OIDC: we can accept either mTLS (client cert) for the VPC endpoint or OIDC token exchange (short-lived JWT) for SDK auth. If you want mTLS, we’ll share CSR/delivery steps.
5) KV/cache and routing: if you plan to pin models by region, include routing metadata in the request path — we’ll provide headers to target the US-prod pool.

Next steps / owners
- Connectiva infra: provision PrivateLink or provide egress CIDRs; confirm by Tue 8/4 (Priya).
- Redwood eng: supply CSR and sample SDK config + a sample schema for structured output (Ben).
- Schedule handoff: technical field-handoff with Redwood infra eng (Marcus) the week of 8/9.

Attachments: I’ve attached a one-page architecture map and a starter mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@connectiva.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna@connectiva.com>, infra@connectiva.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: onramp architecture + networking prerequisites

Thanks, Soojin — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from infra:
- We can do PrivateLink for the dev POC, but prod will need egress-based allowlisting (security constraints). Will that mix break anything on your side?
- For mTLS, our infra prefers issuing client certs from our internal PKI. Can Redwood accept customer-signed certs, or do we need a CA-signed cert from Redwood?
- DNS: we currently manage a private hosted zone; if we point the service hostname to the PrivateLink endpoint, does Redwood need to update any TLS SANs?

Action: I’ve looped infra at infra@connectiva.com — they’ll provide a proposed CIDR and confirm PrivateLink capability by EOD 8/5.

—Priya
Priya Singh
Senior Cloud Engineer, Connectiva Labs
priya.singh@connectiva.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@connectiva.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: onramp architecture + networking prerequisites

Priya — great questions. Short answers:
- PrivateLink + egress allowlist hybrid: supported. For dev we prefer PrivateLink to avoid NAT egress variability; for prod we can accept allowlisted egress IPs. Our runtime will accept both as long as requests authenticate correctly.
- mTLS: Redwood accepts customer-provided client certs signed by your PKI. We will need the cert chain (PEM) and the public CN to map to the tenant identity. We can also support OIDC if you prefer not to manage certs.
- TLS SANs / DNS: if you front with PrivateLink and the hostname resolves to a private IP, no SAN changes required on our side. For egress/allowlist path (public hostname), we serve certs for the public hostname as usual.

I’m attaching a short checklist for the CSR/PKI exchange and a sample SDK snippet showing the mTLS config and OIDC token flow.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-mtls-checklist.txt, sdk-mtls-example.js

From: infra@connectiva.com

Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Connectiva infra: proposed network plan + diagram

Hi Ben and Soojin —

We’ll stand up a PrivateLink endpoint in the dev account. For prod we will provide allowlisted egress CIDRs under a VPC NAT egress pool. Proposed CIDRs (example/dev):
- 10.100.12.0/24 (dev NAT pool)
- 10.100.20.0/28 (private endpoint subnet)

Public egress CIDRs for prod (to be used for allowlist):
- 34.201.45.12/32
- 34.201.45.13/32
- 34.201.45.14/32
- 34.201.45.15/32

We’ve attached an updated network diagram and a short note on how we’ll provision the TLS client certs from our internal PKI (CSR process). Questions:
1) Will Redwood need any additional public IPs for webhook callbacks (tool-calling) or will callbacks be initiated only from Connectiva to Redwood?
2) For embeddings: we want to keep the vector store inside our VPC. What’s the recommended pattern for us hosting a reranker locally and still calling Redwood embeddings?

Thanks,
Connectiva Infra Team
infra@connectiva.com

Attachments: connectiva-network-diagram.png, csr-instructions.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@connectiva.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@connectiva.com>, infra@connectiva.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: onramp architecture + networking prerequisites

Thanks for the plan and the diagram — helpful. Quick answers and proposed schedule: 

1) Webhooks / tool-calling: Redwood can make outbound callbacks for tool invocation. If you prefer callbacks blocked inbound to your app, we can instead implement a polling-based tool sink where your service polls Redwood for actions. For the POC let’s do polling to avoid opening firewall holes.

2) Embeddings and local rerank: Recommended approach:
- Call Redwood embeddings over PrivateLink (dev) / allowlisted egress (prod).
- Store vectors in your VPC-hosted vector DB.
- When re-ranking, send top-N candidates (IDs + vectors) to Redwood rerank endpoint or run your local reranker against the vectors — both are supported. If you want lower latency and full control, local reranker is fine; we’ll provide a binary-compatible scoring hook and a small test harness.

3) Cert exchange: Ben will share an upload link for the cert chain. Please include the cert (PEM), the issuing CA chain, and the CSR CN fields. We’ll map that CN to your tenant and deploy to the dev pool within 24 hours of receipt.

4) Owners & schedule:
- Priya (Connectiva): confirm PrivateLink dev by 8/5 (noted) and prod egress CIDRs by 8/13.
- Redwood (Ben & Marcus): provide mTLS CSR checklist, SDK snippets, and the sample structured output schema by 8/6.
- Handoff: field-handoff call with Redwood infra & Connectiva infra, proposed Wed 8/11 10am PT — Marcus to host.

I’ve attached the mutual_action_plan.xlsx with proposed owners and dates. If that schedule looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite for 8/11.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
